title: Replace the retiring MDI remote-execution alert with a custom detection
problem: Defender for Identity retires the classic 'Remote code execution attempt' (2025) and 'Suspected identity theft (pass-the-hash)' (2036) alerts at the end of November 2026 (MC1552387). Remote execution against DCs and tier-0 servers must move to an advanced hunting custom detection, and pass-the-hash coverage to Defender for Endpoint — without SIEM rules and runbooks silently going quiet.
steps: Inventory dependencies: in Sentinel or your SIEM, find analytics, automation rules, SOAR playbooks and ticket mappings that match the two alert titles or external IDs 2025/2036, and list them with owners.

Open Microsoft's published RemoteCodeExecution query (Microsoft-Defender-for-Identity GitHub). It flags service creation, task scheduling and WMI Win32_Process Create in IdentityDirectoryEvents and suppresses accounts/source devices seen on 3+ of the previous 7 days.

Run it (or the condensed variant on the Code page) over 30 days in advanced hunting and tune: allow-list deployment accounts, monitoring agents and jump hosts by AccountSid or source device rather than by command line.

Make sure the query projects `Timestamp` and `ReportId` from the same event plus an entity column (`AccountSid`/`DeviceName`), and filters on `ingestion_time()` rather than `Timestamp`, as Microsoft recommends for custom detections.
Create the detection rule: unique title, severity, MITRE techniques T1047/T1053.005/T1543.003, frequency of 24 hours or less with a matching time filter, and impacted-entity mapping.

Pass-the-hash: confirm that domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint (Device inventory, onboarding status), since MDE is Microsoft's stated coverage after retirement.
Repoint the SIEM rules and runbooks from step 1 to the new custom detection title, then re-run your remote-execution purple-team test case and record the alert that fires.
pitfalls: The custom detection only sees what the MDI sensors log; missing audit policy or SACLs on a DC means no IdentityDirectoryEvents rows — verify with the DefenderForIdentity module's configuration report.

Microsoft's baseline suppression hides an attacker who reuses an admin account that legitimately runs remote tasks every day; keep a separate, higher-severity rule for tier-0 targets without suppression if volume allows.
Filtering on `Timestamp` in a custom detection can miss late-arriving events; use `ingestion_time()`.
Retirement removes the alert, not historical incidents; closed incidents with the old titles stay searchable for their normal retention.
done_when: A custom detection for remote execution against identity infrastructure is enabled, tuned against 30 days of data and mapped to entities.
Every SIEM rule, playbook and runbook that referenced the two classic alerts is repointed or retired, with an owner recorded.
Tier-0 servers show as onboarded to Defender for Endpoint, and the remote-execution test case produces the new alert.

troubleshooting.symptom: The query returns no rows at all
troubleshooting.cause: No sensor coverage or missing audit configuration on the DCs/servers in scope
troubleshooting.fix: Run `New-MDIConfigurationReport` and `Test-MDIConfiguration -Mode Domain -Configuration All`, fix the reported gaps, then re-run the hunt.

troubleshooting.symptom: Alerts have no impacted asset or wrong scope
troubleshooting.cause: The query does not project ReportId/Timestamp from the same event or an entity identifier
troubleshooting.fix: Project `Timestamp, ReportId` and `AccountSid` or `DeviceName` directly from the matching row; avoid summarize without arg_max.

troubleshooting.symptom: Too many alerts from software deployment
troubleshooting.cause: Deployment or monitoring accounts create services and tasks remotely
troubleshooting.fix: Allow-list by AccountSid or source device, or adopt Microsoft's 7-day baseline suppression from the published query.

rollback: Set the custom detection rule to Off (do not delete it) if it floods the queue, and keep the SIEM rule pointing at it so the gap is visible.
Re-enable after tuning; confirm in the rule's run history that it executes at the chosen frequency.
